items.name: core
items.title: Pi coding agent
items.description: Pi itself, at the version that the kit tested. Each Pi item of this list needs it. Walkr, the Herdr skills and the Claude Code plugin also work without Pi.
items.when_on: Pi sends your conversation to the model provider with your login or key, and a request can cost money. Pi writes sessions and logins into the profile and can download a missing search tool. The installer does not install Pi; install it at the pin first.
items.when_off: No Pi session starts with this profile. Core cannot be turned off.

items.name: model-routing
items.title: Default model settings
items.description: Pi settings for the default provider, model and thinking level, and the model cycle. A provider is the company that runs the model; the cycle is the list that a key steps through.
items.when_on: Pi starts with the default model of the profile.
items.when_off: Pi picks a model itself: the model of a resumed session, a default of the provider or a provider that you logged in to. /model selects another one.

items.name: tenantext
items.title: Tenantext base extension
items.description: The base extension of the Tenantext package: the Simplified English rules, a guard at session start, a context report and the /tenantext settings menu. The other Tenantext items load through the same package entry.
items.when_on: Pi loads the Tenantext package from this clone; keep the clone in its place. The rules go into each prompt to the model provider. It writes its own settings file in the profile.
items.when_off: No Simplified English rules, start guard or context report. The other Tenantext extensions, skills and prompts keep their own switches.

items.name: codex-accounts
items.title: Codex accounts and gateway
items.description: Adds extra Codex accounts, their quota reports and an optional model gateway, a server that forwards model requests.
items.when_on: It reads the Codex login files and sends their tokens and account IDs to the Codex usage endpoint, also without a gateway. With a gateway URL and an API key, from the environment or a stored key, the provider litellm-codex sends your conversation to that gateway. Codex and gateway requests can cost money.
items.when_off: No extra Codex accounts, no Codex quota reports and no gateway provider. Your native provider logins still work.

items.name: context-meter
items.title: Context meter
items.description: Shows how much of the model context the session uses.
items.when_on: It counts the context locally and writes its settings file when you save. With nextMoveUrl set, it sends counters and the last 300 characters of your last message to that URL, with an optional key from the environment. That service can call a decision model, which can cost money.
items.when_off: No context widget. The status footer has its own copy of the meter, so the footer can still show context readings.

items.name: ops-footer
items.title: Status footer
items.description: A footer with the quota, context and health readings.
items.when_on: It polls the health URLs that you set. It runs okknow doctor, which signs in to your OpenKnowledge server, and artifacts status, which asks the local artifacts server on 127.0.0.1. It also runs its own copy of the context meter: with nextMoveUrl set in context-meter/settings.json, it sends counters and the last 300 characters of your last message to that URL, and that service can call a decision model, which can cost money. It writes its settings file and an example file in the profile. Set "enabled": false in ops-footer/settings.json to turn it off.
items.when_off: Pi shows its own footer. No health polls, no runs of okknow or artifacts and no context decisions from the footer. The context-meter extension can still send its own.

items.name: copilot-usage
items.title: Copilot quota meter
items.description: Reads the GitHub Copilot quota of your account. It is on by default; set its mode to off when it must not use your login.
items.when_on: It looks for a Copilot login: the Pi login, an environment variable, the editor login, the Copilot CLI, then gh. It sends the token that it finds to the Copilot usage endpoint. Mode auto shows the meter when that works, on also shows errors, off sends nothing. TENANTEXT_COPILOT_USAGE overrides the mode.
items.when_off: No Copilot quota reading from this meter. /tenantext-doctor can still probe the endpoint when you run it.

items.name: anthropic-usage
items.title: Claude quota meter
items.description: Reads the Claude quota of your Claude login. It is on by default; set its mode to off when it must not use your login.
items.when_on: It reads the Claude Code login, then the Pi anthropic login, and sends the token to the Claude usage endpoint. It writes the reading to a shared cache file, normally ~/.cache/claude-pi-footer/usage.json. Modes auto, on and off work as for the Copilot meter; TENANTEXT_ANTHROPIC_USAGE overrides the mode.
items.when_off: No Claude quota reading from this meter. /tenantext-doctor can still probe the endpoint when you run it.

items.name: doctor
items.title: Setup doctor
items.description: The command /tenantext-doctor checks the setup of the Tenantext extensions. /tenantext-doctor fix repairs it.
items.when_on: The check reads the credential sources of the meters and can send their tokens to the usage endpoints, also for a meter that is off. The fix writes settings files and backups. The fix script of the kit can also add a package entry and repair peer links.
items.when_off: No setup check or repair inside Pi. The meters keep their own switches.

items.name: resources
items.title: Resource switches
items.description: The command /resources turns each extension, skill, prompt and MCP server on or off. An MCP server is a tool server that the agent connects to.
items.when_on: You switch items inside Pi and save sets of states as named profiles. A save writes the filter lists, the named profiles and the enabled state of MCP servers to the files that define them.
items.when_off: No /resources menu. You switch items in settings.json, with /mcp for MCP servers, or with other commands of Pi.

items.name: command-rules
items.title: Command guard
items.description: Blocks a shell command that matches a deny rule and tells the agent why.
items.when_on: For example, find / -name x is refused with a pointer to rg. A bare env or printenv is refused, and only the owner can approve a credsync project. It is not a security boundary.
items.when_off: The agent can run each command that your other settings allow.

items.name: next-prompt
items.title: Next prompt draft
items.description: Shows the next action of the last DUMMIES report as faint text in the empty editor of a coordinator session.
items.when_on: It works only in a coordinator session, with DUMMIES on and its own enabled switch on. Tab takes the draft into the editor. It sends no request.
items.when_off: The editor stays empty after a report. Other editor extensions can still put text there.

items.name: cross-session-recall
items.title: Input history across sessions
items.description: Keeps your typed prompts in one local SQLite store of your user and adds /recall.
items.when_on: Up and Down also show prompts from your other sessions. Only interactive input goes into the store. The store is clear text that only your user can read, with no age or count limit. A pasted secret stays there until /recall-clear.
items.when_off: Each session has only its own input history. The store and its old entries stay on disk.

items.name: hermes
items.title: Hermes local memory
items.description: Local memory: it keeps notes of your sessions as files in the profile.
items.when_on: By default it sends session text to a model for reviews, flushes (a memory save before a compaction or the end of a session), corrections and consolidation (a merge of memory entries when the memory is full), and these calls can cost money. At session start it also indexes the earlier sessions of the profile into its local session database. A config file of its own does not turn the calls off; check its switches.
items.when_off: No local session memory. The stored files stay in the profile.

items.name: wiki
items.title: LLM Wiki vault
items.description: A personal wiki vault in ~/.llm-wiki, outside the profile, that the agent reads and writes. An existing vault keeps its pages, but a session start can add an index folder and a lock file to it, and each write tool updates its index files.
items.when_on: The first start makes the vault and its index files when they are absent. With the default settings, vault text goes into each prompt, and so to the model provider. Ingest makes model calls that can cost money. With an embedding key, pages and queries also go to that embedding service.
items.when_off: No wiki in the sessions. The vault stays on disk.

items.name: openviking
items.title: OpenViking memory
items.description: Sends sessions and memories to an OpenViking server that you set up, and recalls them.
items.when_on: By default each turn goes to that server; tool results go only when you turn that on. The key and the config come from the environment or a config file. A local queue and a recall ledger are shared by your sessions. The server can store and process the text, which can cost money. The installer does not install it; follow the guide.
items.when_off: This extension stops. Other remote memory tools of your setup keep working.

items.name: agentcore
items.title: AgentCore memory
items.description: Shared memory in AWS AgentCore Memory: recall before each prompt and a propose tool that asks you first.
items.when_on: Each typed prompt goes to AWS for recall, and a proposal that you confirm goes there too. It uses your AWS credentials and needs a memory resource in your account; AWS charges for the service. Answers and tool output are not captured. The installer does not install it; follow the guide.
items.when_off: No AWS memory recall and no proposals.

items.name: coordinator-skills
items.title: Coordinator skills
items.description: Skills for a coordinator session: grilling, research, specs, tickets, review and status.
items.when_on: Pi gets the skills. Claude Code gets them only through the links that the installer makes. Some skills run external tools and use GITEA_TOKEN to read and write issues. skill-doctor reads your transcripts and writes report files. The DUMMIES skill can log report text.
items.when_off: No coordinator workflow skills in Pi. The links in ~/.claude/skills stay.

items.name: dummies
items.title: DUMMIES reports
items.description: A coordinator session ends each reply with a short report for a junior developer.
items.when_on: All your Pi profiles share the switch. The autostart block goes into the instruction file of this profile. By default each report is logged: through okknow to the DUMMIES page of the project, else to a local log of your user. The log has its own switch.
items.when_off: Replies have no fixed report form, and the next prompt draft shows nothing. Earlier reports and logs stay.

items.name: knowledge-skills
items.title: OpenKnowledge skills
items.description: Instructions for the agent about OpenKnowledge and the Open Knowledge Format. They are skills, not a server.
items.when_on: The agent knows how to read and write knowledge bundles. Real OpenKnowledge operations need the separate server and client.
items.when_off: No OpenKnowledge guidance from the kit. A skill of the same name in a project stays.

items.name: tracker-site
items.title: Tracker brief
items.description: A skill that builds a short restart brief and a site from the repository and its issue tracker.
items.when_on: It reads the issue API token and sends GET requests to the tracker. It writes the brief and its tracker state, by default under ~/.pi/agent, not in the selected profile. Publishing is optional and uses a login; its receipts hold edit tokens.
items.when_off: No tracker brief.

items.name: okknow
items.title: OpenKnowledge client
items.description: The okknow skill and command for one OpenKnowledge server of yours.
items.when_on: The agent reads and writes pages on that server. The user name and password come from the environment and go only to the configured origin (the scheme, host and port of the server address). The setup probes the origin and writes a user config and local backups. The installer links the command and the Claude Code skill, and can add an MCP entry.
items.when_off: Pi does not load the skill. The command and other harnesses still work.

items.name: artifacts
items.title: Artifact uploads
items.description: The artifacts skill and command: store an HTML or Markdown file in the local artifact store and get a view link of the local artifacts server.
items.when_on: After a secret scan, a file goes into the store ~/.local/share/tenant-artifacts/store of this computer, with scratch files of the scan. The install writes no configuration, needs no token and starts no server. The view link is confidential.
items.when_off: Pi does not load the skill. Other ways to publish a file still work.

items.name: artifacts-prompt
items.title: /artifacts-server command
items.description: A Pi prompt that starts, stops or checks the local artifacts server. It comes with artifacts.
items.when_on: /artifacts-server start runs the read-only artifacts server on 127.0.0.1, port 6790 by default. It needs no token and no login, so each local user of the computer can read the pages. It writes a state file and a log. With a retention set by artifacts retention, it deletes the older artifacts.
items.when_off: You run the artifacts command by hand. A running server does not stop.

items.name: walkr
items.title: Walkr review tool
items.description: The agent prepares a review, you look at it in a browser page, and the agent reads your notes, pick and rating.
items.when_on: The installer links six walkr commands into ~/.local/bin, writes the skills to ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.agents, and downloads missing dependencies. In use, it starts a local web server of your account and keeps sessions and reports on disk. The page URL holds a secret; a bind-all override sends plain HTTP over your network.
items.when_off: Reviews happen in the chat only. Old records stay, and a running server does not stop.

items.name: walkr-prompts
items.title: Walkr commands
items.description: One Pi prompt for each Walkr mode, for example /walkr and /walkr-compare. They come with walkr.
items.when_on: The Walkr setup writes the prompts into the profile.
items.when_off: No Walkr prompts in Pi. The Walkr commands, skills and sessions stay.

items.name: herdr
items.title: Herdr skill
items.description: The skill that starts and drives other agent panes in Herdr. It does not install the Herdr application.
items.when_on: It needs Herdr, Python and its scripts. The agents that it starts get your access and can make paid model calls.
items.when_off: No Herdr guidance for the agent. The Herdr application stays, and agents can still start in other ways. The other Herdr items need this skill.

items.name: herdr-relay
items.title: Herdr relay
items.description: Runs a blocked shell command through a standing worker pane in Herdr.
items.when_on: It needs the herdr skill, or HERDR_SKILL_HOME, and Python. The command runs with the access of the worker pane; this is not a security sandbox. It does nothing until it is used.
items.when_off: The relay is not offered. This does not stop a command from running in another way.

items.name: herdr-watch
items.title: Herdr pane watch
items.description: Starts new task sessions or prompts existing Herdr panes, waits in the background and delivers the reply as a notification.
items.when_on: It needs Herdr, Python and its scripts. It keeps local records of tasks and replies. Work that it starts can make paid model calls.
items.when_off: The agent waits for each pane in the foreground.

items.name: herdr-idle-cleanup
items.title: Idle pane cleanup
items.description: A skill that scans each Herdr workspace, keeps the reports of idle panes and closes them after your yes.
items.when_on: A scan writes scan.json, and the reports go to handoff files under ~/.local/share/tenant-pi/handoffs. publish --upload sends report text with a configured token.
items.when_off: No scan from the skill. Its scripts and old handoff files stay. The handoff check and its command need this skill.

items.name: handoffs
items.title: Handoff check at start
items.description: The startup check of the idle pane cleanup, with /handoffs and /herdr-idle.
items.when_on: At the start of a new interactive session, it claims the open handoff entries of the repository and writes their state. A claimed entry can start one assessment model turn, which can cost money. Task sessions and reloads claim nothing. /herdr-idle shows the state; /herdr-idle off turns the check off.
items.when_off: No check at session start and no assessment turn.

items.name: herdr-idle-cleanup-prompt
items.title: /herdr-idle-cleanup command
items.description: A Pi prompt that loads the idle pane cleanup skill and runs its default run.
items.when_on: /herdr-idle-cleanup is a command in Pi.
items.when_off: Only this shortcut goes. The skill and its scripts still work; ask for the skill in plain words.

items.name: questions
items.title: Question tool
items.description: Gives Pi the ask_user_question tool. The core install adds it.
items.when_on: Skills can ask you questions with choices in an interactive Pi session. It reads shared user guidance outside the selected profile.
items.when_off: Skills ask in plain text. A session without a terminal has no question dialog in either case.

items.name: mcp
items.title: MCP adapter
items.description: Connects MCP servers through pi-mcp-adapter. MCP is a standard connection between the agent and tool servers.
items.when_on: It starts the commands of your server file or connects to its endpoints, and configured credential and header helpers can run. OAuth and bearer tokens go to the keyring of the system, and large results can go to temporary files. What a server does and costs depends on its configuration. The adapter replaces the MCP support of Pi.
items.when_off: No MCP servers through the adapter. The -builtin:mcp entry that the adapter wrote can stay and keep the MCP support of Pi off.

items.name: mcp-codemode
items.title: MCP with codemode
items.description: The MCP client of Pi and its codemode tool, without the adapter. In codemode, the model writes scripts that call the tools. For a comparison profile.
items.when_on: The installer adds +codemode to defaultTools and removes the adapter entry, -builtin:mcp and -builtin:codemode. It does not convert the server file of the adapter. At session start, Pi connects to each enabled server of mcp.json; a server with "enabled": false gets no connection. The servers get the credentials of their configuration: environment values, headers, OAuth tokens or a provider login. A script that the model writes runs when the model calls the codemode tool, and it can call each tool of the connected servers. What a server does with the data and what it costs depends on the server.
items.when_off: The installer changes nothing. Pi still turns codemode on for an enabled server with codemode exposure (the server setting that makes its tools callable only from codemode scripts, the default), and its MCP client stays on unless -builtin:mcp is set.

items.name: computer-use
items.title: Computer use on Linux
items.description: Tools that read the screen and send clicks, keys and text to your Linux desktop.
items.when_on: Screenshots and screen text go into the conversation, and so to the model provider. The setup downloads a release binary. It needs a graphical session, AT-SPI and an input backend, and its setup tools can change desktop settings.
items.when_off: This Pi module does not load. Other desktop tools of your system stay.

items.name: computer-use-macos
items.title: Computer use on macOS
items.description: Tools that read the screen and send input to your Mac through Cua Driver, on macOS 13 or later. Not verified on a Mac.
items.when_on: Screenshots, screen text and typed text go to the model provider. Cua Driver sends telemetry by default. At the first desktop tool call, the driver starts and macOS asks for Accessibility and Screen Recording. The core tool profile is not an allowlist, and a yes to an app launch is not a yes to each action.
items.when_off: The agent cannot see or control your Mac through this module.

items.name: claude-code-plugin
items.title: Claude Code desktop plugin
items.description: The computer-use-linux plugin for Claude Code, from its own marketplace.
items.when_on: It needs its own yes. The marketplace and the install use the network, and the first start downloads a binary to a cache. Screenshots and screen text go to the model provider. New Claude Code sessions get the desktop tools, except read-role panes. The marketplace version can be newer than the kit pin.
items.when_off: Claude Code has no tools from this plugin. Other plugins stay.

items.name: shell-rc
items.title: Shell alias
items.description: A marked block with an alias for the launcher of the profile, in ~/.bashrc, or in .zshrc in ZDOTDIR or your home.
items.when_on: You type the profile name to start Pi with this profile. The installer backs up the file first.
items.when_off: No alias. You run the launcher directly, or start Pi with PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR set.

items.name: launcher
items.title: Profile launcher
items.description: A small script in ~/.local/bin that starts the selected runtime with this profile.
items.when_on: It sets the profile and PATH, clears an inherited session directory and can start through the credsync launch wrapper. It records the runtime path; run an upgrade after you move Pi, Pi-Bolt or Node. It keeps configurations apart; it is not an OS sandbox.
items.when_off: No launcher; you start Pi by hand.
